Purpose: To make sure that one run at a time works in a workspace, and to tell a live owner from a dead one.
Caller and time: The runtime root (the engine in start mode `standalone`) at launch, at a heartbeat, at the end.
The engine at every boundary (`verify`). The CLI and the doctor (`probe`). `resume` (`reclaim`).
Inputs: `acquire`: the scope (the workspace) and the owner record of annex B §B.9. `heartbeat`,
`release`: the lease. `probe`, `reclaim`: the scope. `handDown`: the lease. `verify`: a token.
Outputs: `acquire`: a lease, or a conflict that names the holder. `probe`: one of the closed set `free`,

Errors: `conflict` (engine code 5, pipeline code 24); `foreign-owner`, which is never reclaimed
Guarantees of the core: One run per workspace. The scope is the workspace. A lease is handed down, so a child never takes
a second lock. `owner-dead-group-alive` refuses a start and names the survivors; `adoptable`
processes never cause it. A signal is sent only when pid, start time and run token all match. The
provider in use is recorded in the workspace record; a different provider refuses.
Guarantees of an implementation: Exclusion is atomic. A lock never exists without its owner record. Reclaim is atomic and never a
removal followed by a creation. Liveness rests on something the kernel releases when the owner
dies. Behaviour is the same on Linux and macOS. No component is compiled at install.
Failure of an implementation: A provider that fails in `acquire` or `probe` gives `unknown`, which counts as held: the launch is

Unknown-value rule: An unknown result of `probe` is read as `unknown`. An owner record with an unknown field is
accepted; one that lacks a required field is `unknown`.
Wave 1 implementations: One provider: a directory lock with the owner record renamed into place, reclaim by rename, and
liveness backed by the kernel through something the runtime platform ships.
